title: Paul before Felix: Tertullus's accusation + Paul's defense and two years' imprisonment

paragraphs.text: And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with certain elders, and [with] an orator, one Tertullus; and they informed the governor against Paul.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ δὲ πέντε ἡμέρας κατέβη ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἁνανίας μετὰ πρεσβυτέρων τινῶν καὶ ῥήτορος Τερτύλλου τινός, οἵτινες ἐνεφάνισαν τῷ ἡγεμόνι κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου.
paragraphs.translit: Meta de pente hēmeras katebē ho archiereus Hananias meta presbyterōn tinōn kai rhētoros Tertyllou tinos, hoitines enephanisan tō hēgemoni kata tou Paulou.

paragraphs.text: And when he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy much peace, and that by the providence evils are corrected for this nation,
paragraphs.original: κληθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἤρξατο κατηγορεῖν ὁ Τέρτυλλος λέγων· Πολλῆς εἰρήνης τυγχάνοντες διὰ σοῦ καὶ διορθωμάτων γινομένων τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ διὰ τῆς σῆς προνοίας
paragraphs.translit: klēthentos de autou ērxato katēgorein ho Tertyllos legōn· Pollēs eirēnēs tynchanontes dia sou kai diorthōmatōn ginomenōn tō ethnei toutō dia tēs sēs pronoias

paragraphs.text: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
paragraphs.original: πάντῃ τε καὶ πανταχοῦ ἀποδεχόμεθα, κράτιστε Φῆλιξ, μετὰ πάσης εὐχαριστίας.
paragraphs.translit: pantē te kai pantachou apodechometha, kratiste Phēlix, meta pasēs eucharistias.

paragraphs.text: But, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I entreat thee to hear us of thy clemency a few words.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα δὲ μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖόν σε ἐγκόπτω, παρακαλῶ ἀκοῦσαί σε ἡμῶν συντόμως τῇ σῇ ἐπιεικείᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: hina de mē epi pleion se enkoptō, parakalō akousai se hēmōn syntomōs tē sē epieikeia.

paragraphs.text: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
paragraphs.original: εὑρόντες γὰρ τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον λοιμὸν καὶ κινοῦντα στάσεις πᾶσι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τοῖς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην πρωτοστάτην τε τῆς τῶν Ναζωραίων αἱρέσεως,
paragraphs.translit: heurontes gar ton andra touton loimon kai kinounta staseis pasi tois Ioudaiois tois kata tēn oikoumenēn prōtostatēn te tēs tōn Nazōraiōn haireseōs,

paragraphs.text: who moreover assayed to profane the temple: on whom also we laid hold: [and we would have judged him according to our law.]
paragraphs.original: ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπείρασεν βεβηλῶσαι, ὃν καὶ ἐκρατήσαμεν,
paragraphs.translit: hos kai to hieron epeirasen bebēlōsai, hon kai ekratēsamen,

paragraphs.text: [But the chief captain Lysias came, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,]
[commanding his accusers to come before thee.] from whom thou wilt be able, by examining him thyself, to take knowledge of all these things whereof we accuse him.
paragraphs.original: παρʼ οὗ δυνήσῃ αὐτὸς ἀνακρίνας περὶ πάντων τούτων ἐπιγνῶναι ὧν ἡμεῖς κατηγοροῦμεν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: parʼ hou dynēsē autos anakrinas peri pantōn toutōn epignōnai hōn hēmeis katēgoroumen autou.

paragraphs.text: And the Jews also joined in the charge, affirming that these things were so.
paragraphs.original: συνεπέθεντο δὲ καὶ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι φάσκοντες ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχειν.
paragraphs.translit: synepethento de kai hoi Ioudaioi phaskontes tauta houtōs echein.

paragraphs.text: And when the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, Paul answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I cheerfully make my defense:
paragraphs.original: Ἀπεκρίθη τε ὁ Παῦλος νεύσαντος αὐτῷ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος λέγειν· Ἐκ πολλῶν ἐτῶν ὄντα σε κριτὴν τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ ἐπιστάμενος εὐθύμως τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἀπολογοῦμαι,
paragraphs.translit: Apekrithē te ho Paulos neusantos autō tou hēgemonos legein· Ek pollōn etōn onta se kritēn tō ethnei toutō epistamenos euthymōs ta peri emautou apologoumai,

paragraphs.text: Seeing that thou canst take knowledge that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem:
paragraphs.original: δυναμένου σου ἐπιγνῶναι, ὅτι οὐ πλείους εἰσίν μοι ἡμέραι δώδεκα ἀφʼ ἧς ἀνέβην προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,
paragraphs.translit: dynamenou sou epignōnai, hoti ou pleious eisin moi hēmerai dōdeka aphʼ hēs anebēn proskynēsōn eis Ierousalēm,

paragraphs.text: and neither in the temple did they find me disputing with any man or stirring up a crowd, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὔτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ εὗρόν με πρός τινα διαλεγόμενον ἢ ἐπίστασιν ποιοῦντα ὄχλου οὔτε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς οὔτε κατὰ τὴν πόλιν,
paragraphs.translit: kai oute en tō hierō heuron me pros tina dialegomenon ē epistasin poiounta ochlou oute en tais synagōgais oute kata tēn polin,

paragraphs.text: Neither can they prove to thee the things whereof they now accuse me.
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ παραστῆσαι δύνανταί σοι περὶ ὧν νυνὶ κατηγοροῦσίν μου.
paragraphs.translit: oude parastēsai dynantai soi peri hōn nyni katēgorousin mou.

paragraphs.text: But this I confess unto thee, that after the Way which they call a sect, so serve I the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;
paragraphs.original: ὁμολογῶ δὲ τοῦτό σοι ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἣν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν οὕτως λατρεύω τῷ πατρῴῳ θεῷ, πιστεύων πᾶσι τοῖς κατὰ τὸν νόμον καὶ τοῖς ἐν τοῖς προφήταις γεγραμμένοις,
paragraphs.translit: homologō de touto soi hoti kata tēn hodon hēn legousin hairesin houtōs latreuō tō patrōō theō, pisteuōn pasi tois kata ton nomon kai tois en tois prophētais gegrammenois,

paragraphs.text: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there shall be a resurrection both of the just and unjust.
paragraphs.original: ἐλπίδα ἔχων εἰς τὸν θεόν, ἣν καὶ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι προσδέχονται, ἀνάστασιν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι δικαίων τε καὶ ἀδίκων·
paragraphs.translit: elpida echōn eis ton theon, hēn kai autoi houtoi prosdechontai, anastasin mellein esesthai dikaiōn te kai adikōn·

paragraphs.text: Herein I also exercise myself to have a conscience void of offence toward God and men always.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τούτῳ καὶ αὐτὸς ἀσκῶ ἀπρόσκοπον συνείδησιν ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους διὰ παντός.
paragraphs.translit: en toutō kai autos askō aproskopon syneidēsin echein pros ton theon kai tous anthrōpous dia pantos.

paragraphs.text: Now after some years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings:
paragraphs.original: διʼ ἐτῶν δὲ πλειόνων ἐλεημοσύνας ποιήσων εἰς τὸ ἔθνος μου παρεγενόμην καὶ προσφοράς,
paragraphs.translit: diʼ etōn de pleionōn eleēmosynas poiēsōn eis to ethnos mou paregenomēn kai prosphoras,

paragraphs.text: amidst which they found me purified in the temple, with no crowd, nor yet with tumult: but [there were] certain Jews from Asia--
paragraphs.original: ἐν αἷς εὗρόν με ἡγνισμένον ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, οὐ μετὰ ὄχλου οὐδὲ μετὰ θορύβου,
paragraphs.translit: en hais heuron me hēgnismenon en tō hierō, ou meta ochlou oude meta thorybou,

paragraphs.text: who ought to have been here before thee, and to make accusation, if they had aught against me.
paragraphs.original: τινὲς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι, οὓς ἔδει ἐπὶ σοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ κατηγορεῖν εἴ τι ἔχοιεν πρὸς ἐμέ,
paragraphs.translit: tines de apo tēs Asias Ioudaioi, hous edei epi sou pareinai kai katēgorein ei ti echoien pros eme,

paragraphs.text: Or else let these men themselves say what wrong-doing they found when I stood before the council,
paragraphs.original: ἢ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι εἰπάτωσαν τί εὗρον ἀδίκημα στάντος μου ἐπὶ τοῦ συνεδρίου
paragraphs.translit: ē autoi houtoi eipatōsan ti heuron adikēma stantos mou epi tou synedriou

paragraphs.text: except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question before you this day.
paragraphs.original: ἢ περὶ μιᾶς ταύτης φωνῆς ἧς ἐκέκραξα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἑστὼς ὅτι Περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι σήμερον ἐφʼ ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ē peri mias tautēs phōnēs hēs ekekraxa en autois hestōs hoti Peri anastaseōs nekrōn egō krinomai sēmeron ephʼ hymōn.

paragraphs.text: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will determine your matter.
paragraphs.original: Ἀνεβάλετο δὲ αὐτοὺς ὁ Φῆλιξ, ἀκριβέστερον εἰδὼς τὰ περὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ, εἴπας· Ὅταν Λυσίας ὁ χιλίαρχος καταβῇ διαγνώσομαι τὰ καθʼ ὑμᾶς·
paragraphs.translit: Anebaleto de autous ho Phēlix, akribesteron eidōs ta peri tēs hodou, eipas· Hotan Lysias ho chiliarchos katabē diagnōsomai ta kathʼ hymas·

paragraphs.text: And he gave order to the centurion that he should be kept in charge, and should have indulgence; and not to forbid any of his friends to minister unto him.
paragraphs.original: διαταξάμενος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἔχειν τε ἄνεσιν καὶ μηδένα κωλύειν τῶν ἰδίων αὐτοῦ ὑπηρετεῖν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: diataxamenos tō hekatontarchē tēreisthai auton echein te anesin kai mēdena kōlyein tōn idiōn autou hypēretein autō.

paragraphs.text: But after certain days, Felix came with Drusilla, his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ δὲ ἡμέρας τινὰς παραγενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ σὺν Δρουσίλλῃ τῇ ἰδίᾳ γυναικὶ οὔσῃ Ἰουδαίᾳ μετεπέμψατο τὸν Παῦλον καὶ ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ περὶ τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν πίστεως.
paragraphs.translit: Meta de hēmeras tinas paragenomenos ho Phēlix syn Drousillē tē idia gynaiki ousē Ioudaia metepempsato ton Paulon kai ēkousen autou peri tēs eis Christon Iēsoun pisteōs.

paragraphs.text: And as he reasoned of righteousness, and self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, Go thy way for this time; and when I have a convenient season, I will call thee unto me.
paragraphs.original: διαλεγομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἐγκρατείας καὶ τοῦ κρίματος τοῦ μέλλοντος ἔμφοβος γενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ ἀπεκρίθη· Τὸ νῦν ἔχον πορεύου, καιρὸν δὲ μεταλαβὼν μετακαλέσομαί σε·
paragraphs.translit: dialegomenou de autou peri dikaiosynēs kai enkrateias kai tou krimatos tou mellontos emphobos genomenos ho Phēlix apekrithē· To nyn echon poreuou, kairon de metalabōn metakalesomai se·

paragraphs.text: He hoped withal that money would be given him of Paul: wherefore also he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
paragraphs.original: ἅμα καὶ ἐλπίζων ὅτι χρήματα δοθήσεται αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου· διὸ καὶ πυκνότερον αὐτὸν μεταπεμπόμενος ὡμίλει αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: hama kai elpizōn hoti chrēmata dothēsetai autō hypo tou Paulou· dio kai pyknoteron auton metapempomenos hōmilei autō.

paragraphs.text: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus; and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.
paragraphs.original: Διετίας δὲ πληρωθείσης ἔλαβεν διάδοχον ὁ Φῆλιξ Πόρκιον Φῆστον· θέλων τε χάριτα καταθέσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὁ Φῆλιξ κατέλιπε τὸν Παῦλον δεδεμένον.
paragraphs.translit: Dietias de plērōtheisēs elaben diadochon ho Phēlix Porkion Phēston· thelōn te charita katathesthai tois Ioudaiois ho Phēlix katelipe ton Paulon dedemenon.
